exposure: sampling location (fetal membranes, umbilical cord, chorionic villi)
analytical method (bacterial culture, qPCR, shotgun metagenomics)
mode of birth (cesarean section, vaginal delivery)
cohort: Healthy pregnant women (n = 38) recruited in three maternity wards.
finding: The study found that meaningful quantities of viable bacteria or bacterial DNA were isolated only outside the placenta (fetal membranes and umbilical cords), concluding that the placenta does not harbor a specific, consistent, and functional microbiota.
cross-section timing: At the time of birth (after cesarean section or vaginal delivery)
